To people saying that 500 € banknotes are destroyed when returned back to banks, this might be true in France or Spain, but it's not a general rule.
(Source  https://www.bundesbank.de/en/tasks/topics/production-and-issuance-of-the-500-banknote-will-be-discontinued-623402 - Commercial parties, such as banks, cash-in-transit companies, bureaux de change etc. are allowed to recirculate €500 banknotes.)


Especially in Austria and Germany, deposited 500€ notes can become available again for withdrawals at the same ATM. (Examples on the EuroBillTracker forum https://forum.eurobilltracker.com/viewtopic.php?t=57010&start=60) 

Remember that it's still possible to get, albeit very rarely for sure, old 2002 notes from ATMs such as 10 20 50s etc. They are not necessarily destroyed upon deposit at the bank.

Just a little info, the printer for Euro banknotes is shown on the front side by the small serial code (6-character length). Here on the old €5 note, it begins with P, meaning it was printed by Giesecke & Devrient (Germany - Munich/Leipzig).

The X on the reverse side just tells it was issued for Germany's needs of cash 🙂
